A.vi: Giới thiệu bản thân
cau: Hi there!
So, my name is Son — I'm 23 years old and I work as a software engineer at gemini Vietnam's R&D Center here in Hanoi.
My job mainly involves developing mobile applications and working closely with Korean engineers, so I actually use English quite a bit on a daily basis.
Outside of work... I like to keep things pretty simple, honestly.
I go jogging in the mornings, watch movies when I have the time, and I really enjoy exploring new cafes around the city.
I'd describe myself as a fairly calm and detail-oriented person — which, I think, fits pretty well with software development.
Yeah, that's basically me in a nutshell.
Thanks for asking!

A.vi: Miêu tả 2 người trong gia đình/bạn bè – điểm giống và khác nhau
cau: Sure!
I'd love to talk about two people who are really close to me — my younger brother and my best friend Minh.
My brother is 25, works as a teacher, and honestly he's the kind of person who can light up any room — super outgoing, talkative, always in a good mood.
Minh, on the other hand, is around my age and works in finance.
He's a lot quieter and more reserved — kind of the opposite personality.
But what's interesting is that despite those differences, they actually have a lot in common.
Both of them love being active — they jog and cycle regularly on weekends.
And they're both incredibly dependable.
Whenever I need advice or just someone to talk to, I know I can count on either of them.
I think having both types of people in my life has actually been really good for me — they balance each other out in a nice way.

A.vi: Khi nói chuyện với bạn bè thường nói về vấn đề gì?
cau: Hmm, when I hang out or call my friends, we usually end up talking about all sorts of things, to be honest.
Work is probably the most common topic — we swap stories about our jobs, funny office situations, or sometimes ask each other for career advice.
We also talk a lot about movies and shows.
Since I'm pretty into films, I'll often recommend something and then we'll share our thoughts afterward.
Tech comes up a fair amount too, especially since a lot of my close friends work in tech-related areas.
And sometimes — not always, but sometimes — we get into deeper stuff, like life goals, travel plans, or just... venting about a stressful week.
Honestly, I think good conversations with friends are one of the best ways to recharge and get a fresh perspective on things.

A.vi: Chủ đề khi gặp gia đình/bạn bè và ảnh hưởng của việc sống chung
cau: When I get together with family or friends, the conversations are usually pretty lively and cover a lot of ground.
With family, we catch up on the everyday stuff — how work's going, what we've been eating, any news about relatives.
With friends it tends to be more about shared interests — movies, sports, travel plans, that kind of thing.
In terms of living together — I used to live with my family before I moved to Hanoi for work.
And that really shaped me, I think.
It taught me to be more considerate, to communicate openly, and to share responsibilities.
Now that I live alone, I do sometimes miss that energy.
But living on my own has also given me a real sense of independence and self-discipline, which I genuinely value.

A.vi: Tính cách của hai người trong gia đình/bạn bè: điểm chung và khác biệt
cau: So, comparing my brother and Minh in terms of personality — they're actually quite different.
My brother is naturally extroverted — enthusiastic, sociable, always looking for the next thing to do or talk about.
Minh is more introverted and thoughtful.
He's the type who listens carefully before he speaks, which I really respect.
One big thing they share, though, is loyalty.
Both of them are genuinely trustworthy — neither would ever let a friend down.
They're also both really hardworking in their own fields, which I find admirable.
The biggest difference is probably how they handle pressure.
My brother stays upbeat and energetic, while Minh gets calm and analytical.
I think both approaches have their strengths.

A.vi: Điều tồi tệ xảy ra với gia đình hoặc bất đồng với gia đình
cau: One really difficult period for my family was when my grandfather became seriously ill a few years ago.
He had to be hospitalized for several weeks, and the whole family was really worried.
My parents took turns staying at the hospital, which was exhausting — both physically and emotionally.
During that time, there were some disagreements about which hospital to go to and what treatment options to pursue.
Those kinds of tensions are pretty normal under stress, I think.
But in the end, we managed to come to an agreement through open family discussion.
Thankfully, my grandfather did recover after a few months.
And honestly, going through that together brought our family closer.
It really showed us how important communication is when things get hard.

A.vi: Chọn một mâu thuẫn với cha mẹ và kể chi tiết
cau: The biggest disagreement I've had with my parents was about my career path after I graduated.
They really wanted me to find a stable government job close to our hometown — they were worried about job security and, I think, about the distance if I moved to Hanoi.
But I was passionate about working in tech.
I'd already received an offer from gemini, and I knew it was the right move for me.
We had several long conversations about it — some of them got a bit heated, to be honest.
But I could tell they were coming from a place of genuine concern, not trying to control me.
I tried to explain my reasoning — that the tech industry has strong prospects, and gemini is a well- respected company.
After a few weeks of back-and-forth, they agreed to support my decision.
And looking back, I'm really grateful for how it turned out — and for how that experience helped us communicate more openly as a family.

A.vi: Miêu tả nhà của bạn / miêu tả chi tiết ngôi nhà đang sống
cau: So right now, I'm living in a one-bedroom apartment on the 8th floor of a residential building in Cau Giay District, Hanoi.
I live by myself, which was a conscious choice — I like having a quiet, focused space after a full day of coding and meetings.
The apartment has a living room that opens into a small kitchen, one bedroom, and a bathroom.
It's compact, but everything's there.
In the living room, there's a sofa, a TV, and a small bookshelf.
The kitchen is pretty basic — I mainly use it for coffee and simple meals.
My bedroom is probably my favorite part.
It has a comfortable bed, a desk by the window, and a wardrobe.
The location is also really convenient — close to my office, supermarkets, and a nearby park.
Overall, I'm quite happy with it.

A.vi: Miêu tả phòng trong ngôi nhà yêu thích
cau: Definitely my bedroom — no question there.
It's a relatively small room, but I've set it up to be as cozy and functional as possible.
There's a king-sized bed with really soft pillows, which I genuinely look forward to every evening after work.
Next to the bed is a wooden desk by the window, where I sit to work or read while looking out at the city.
In the evenings, the view of the city lights is honestly really calming.
I also keep a Bluetooth speaker on the desk, so I usually put on some soft music before going to sleep.
It's quiet, it's personal, and whenever I feel stressed, just lying down in that room and listening to music instantly helps me reset.

A.vi: So sánh nhà ở quá khứ và hiện tại
cau: My current place is really quite different from the house I grew up in.
When I was young, we lived in a two-story house in a smaller city — spacious, with a front yard, a big kitchen, and everyone had their own room.
The surroundings were peaceful — trees, neighbors who knew each other, fresh air in the mornings.
It was lovely.
Now I'm in a small one-bedroom apartment in the city with no outdoor space, which I do miss sometimes.
But the location is hard to beat — I'm close to everything I need: work, restaurants, cafes, a park.
The city noise can get a bit much at times, but overall, I appreciate the convenience.
Both places have their charm, and I carry good memories from my childhood home.

A.vi: Miêu tả nhà, phòng thích nhất và sự thay đổi đồ đạc trong nhà
cau: My apartment's layout is simple — living room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom.
The bedroom is definitely my sanctuary.
When I first moved in, the apartment came with very basic furnishings — pretty bare, honestly.
Over the past two years I've gradually made it feel more like home.
The biggest purchase was probably a new ergonomic desk chair, because I spend a lot of hours working from home and my back was suffering.
I also got a small bookshelf and some indoor plants to make the living room feel warmer.
Most recently I replaced my old mattress with a better quality one, and the difference in sleep quality has been noticeable.
I like the idea of slowly improving the space over time — it doesn't need to be perfect all at once.

A.vi: Nếu mua đồ nội thất mới: mua ở đâu, cách tìm như thế nào?
cau: If I needed to buy new furniture, I'd always start by researching online first before going to any store.
I usually check platforms like Tiki or Lazada, compare prices, and read through customer reviews.
For smaller things like shelves or lamps, buying online is fine as long as the reviews are solid.
For bigger items — a sofa, a bed frame — I prefer going to a physical store to see the quality and size for myself.
There's a furniture store near my area I've visited a couple of times and found pretty good.
I also browse Instagram and Pinterest for design inspiration before I decide on anything.
My main priorities are always durability, functionality, and whether it fits both the room and my budget.
Good furniture is worth investing in — it directly affects how comfortable your everyday life is.

A.vi: Nếu thiết kế lại phòng: cách thức và lý do
cau: If I could redesign my bedroom, I'd start by repainting the walls — probably a soft warm tone like light beige or sage green, instead of the plain white they are now.
I think color really does affect mood, and something warmer would make the room feel a lot cozier.
I'd also rearrange the furniture a bit.
Right now my desk placement is a bit awkward — I'd move it to get better natural light.
I'd add some wall shelving to store books and decorative items without taking up floor space.
And better blackout curtains, definitely — the current ones let in way too much light in the morning.
The main goal is to create a space that's both restful and inspiring — somewhere I can properly relax, but also focus when I need to.

A.vi: Trang trí bên ngoài ngôi nhà
cau: Since I'm in an apartment building, I don't really have control over the exterior.
But I do have a small balcony, and I've tried to make it a nice little space.
I put a couple of potted plants out there — a cactus and a small fern — because they're easy to look after and add a bit of greenery.
I also have a folding chair out there.
On nice evenings, I'll sit outside with a coffee and enjoy the view.
It's a small thing, but it makes a difference.
If I owned a house someday, I'd definitely put more time and effort into proper garden and exterior design.

A.vi: Vấn đề tại nơi bạn sống / cách giải quyết
cau: Living in an apartment building comes with a few recurring issues.
The most persistent one is noise — the building's on a fairly busy street, so I can hear traffic, especially at night.
I started using earplugs when I sleep, and honestly it's helped a lot.
Another issue was when the water heater broke down last winter.
I had to take cold showers for about three days, which was pretty miserable.
I reported it to building management and they got a technician in within two days, so that was resolved fairly quickly.
There was also a week when the elevator was out of service — so eight flights of stairs, every single day.
That one was painful.
For these kinds of problems, I've found the best approach is just to report them to management promptly and follow up if they're taking too long.

A.vi: Vấn đề nơi bạn sống: họp gia đình bàn bạc, cách giải quyết
cau: When I still lived with my family, we'd occasionally have to sit down together to discuss household problems.
One of the more serious ones was when the roof started leaking during the rainy season — it was affecting multiple rooms and the humidity was damaging some furniture.
My dad wanted to fix it immediately; my mum was more concerned about the cost.
That kind of disagreement is pretty natural.
After talking it through at dinner, we agreed to hire a professional contractor to do a proper repair rather than a quick patch-up.
It took about two weeks, but the result was much better than we expected.
That experience really showed me how important it is to tackle household problems quickly — and as a team.

A.vi: Thể loại âm nhạc yêu thích? Ca sĩ / nhạc sĩ yêu thích?
cau: Music is a pretty big part of my day-to-day life.
My favorite genre is probably indie pop and acoustic music — I find it really soothing without being boring.
My favorite Vietnamese artist is Ha Anh Tuan.
He has a warm, emotional voice and his songs are about everyday feelings in a really relatable way.
I also enjoy Ed Sheeran from time to time — his songwriting is very natural and conversational, which I appreciate.
I usually listen on Spotify — during my morning jog, on the commute, or before sleeping.
Music has this incredible ability to shift your mood almost instantly.
After a long day, putting on a calm playlist helps me unwind really quickly.

A.vi: Thể loại nhạc yêu thích? Trước đây và bây giờ có thay đổi không?
cau: Definitely, my taste has changed a lot over the years.
Back in middle and high school, I mainly listened to popular Vietnamese pop and K-pop — basically whatever was trending at the time.
I didn't really have a strong personal preference; I just followed what my friends liked.
Then at university, living more independently, I started exploring on YouTube and discovered indie pop, lo-fi beats, and acoustic folk music.
I immediately connected with them — they felt more personal somehow.
Now my everyday playlist is mostly soft indie songs, gentle jazz, and lo-fi music for working or studying.
I think the shift reflects how my lifestyle changed — from a social, school-based life to something more introspective and focused.

A.vi: Âm nhạc hồi bé và hiện tại, tác giả/ca khúc ưa thích
cau: When I was young, I didn't really pay much attention to music intentionally — I just heard whatever was on TV or at family gatherings.
I remember my mother humming old Vietnamese folk songs while cooking.
Those melodies still feel really nostalgic to me.
As I got older — especially in high school — I started exploring on my own and discovered artists like Son Tung MTP and some K-pop groups.
Now, my taste has matured quite a bit.
My current favorite is Ha Anh Tuan's album 'Trinh Ca'.
His songs are poetic, emotionally layered, and beautifully arranged with acoustic instruments.
Listening to his music kind of feels like reading a short story — there's always a mood and a narrative being told.
The shift from childhood music to now reflects how my appreciation for depth and craftsmanship has grown.

A.vi: Lần đầu nghe nhạc với ai, ở đâu, phương pháp nghe nhạc
cau: My earliest memory of really listening to music was when I was about 10.
My dad had an old CD player in the living room, and in the evenings he'd play Vietnamese ballads.
I remember sitting with him and just... listening together.
I didn't fully understand the lyrics, but the music felt comforting somehow.
That was also when I first noticed how music could set an atmosphere and create emotion in a room.
As I got older, I moved from MP3 players to smartphones, and now I stream everything on Spotify.
These days, I prefer listening through wireless earphones — usually during my morning jog or when I'm doing focused work.
Good earphones really do make a difference in the listening experience.
And that early memory of listening with my dad is something I still think about fondly.

A.vi: Bắt đầu thích nghe nhạc như thế nào? Sự thay đổi sở thích theo thời gian
cau: I became a more conscious music listener during my first year of university.
Before that, music was mostly background noise — I wasn't really stopping to actually listen.
But when I started living in a dormitory away from home, music became a way to cope with homesickness and stress.
I'd put on headphones and just explore different artists for hours.
That's when I discovered acoustic guitar music, and I fell in love with the simplicity and intimacy of it.
Over the years, my preferences shifted from energetic pop to slower, more thoughtful genres.
Now music is a daily thing for me — and it's become an important emotional outlet.
It helps me process feelings that I might not easily put into words.

A.vi: Bộ phim yêu thích của bạn là gì?
cau: My all-time favorite movie is Interstellar, directed by Christopher Nolan.
It's a sci-fi film that manages to combine really complex ideas about space, time, and physics with an incredibly emotional story — a father trying to save his daughter and humanity.
What I love most is how it's both intellectually stimulating and deeply moving at the same time.
That's not easy to pull off.
The visual effects are breathtaking — especially the scenes depicting black holes.
And the Hans Zimmer soundtrack is one of the best I've ever heard.
I've watched it three times now, and each time I notice something new.
For me, a great movie is one that stays with you long after it ends — and Interstellar definitely does that.

A.vi: Thể loại phim yêu thích / thể loại phim xem gần đây
cau: My favorite genres are sci-fi and psychological thrillers — I'm really drawn to stories that challenge the way you think.
Sci-fi lets me explore big questions about space, technology, and the future in an entertaining way.
Thrillers keep me hooked because of the tension and unpredictability.
Recently I've also been watching more Korean films and dramas, which tend to have really strong storytelling and character development.
I watched Parasite last year and was completely blown away — the layered social commentary, the plot twists... just incredible.
On weekends, I usually watch a movie or a couple of episodes of something at home.
I think good films are one of the most efficient ways to learn about different cultures and the human experience.

A.vi: Đi xem phim cùng bạn thường làm gì?
cau: Going to the cinema with friends is always a great time from start to finish.
We usually plan a few days ahead — figure out what to watch and book tickets online to avoid the queue.
Before the movie, we almost always grab a meal first, usually at a nearby restaurant or food court.
At the cinema, I always get a medium popcorn and a drink — that's just a non-negotiable ritual for me.
Can't skip it.
During the film we stay quiet, but you can always feel the group's reactions — laughing together or gasping at the same moment.
That shared experience is really something.
After, we usually find a café nearby and talk about the film.
Those post-movie discussions are honestly my favorite part — everyone has different observations and interpretations.

A.vi: Sự kiện trước/sau khi xem phim tại rạp
cau: A typical cinema trip for me follows a pretty enjoyable routine.
First, I research the film — read a brief synopsis and watch the trailer to decide if it's worth the big screen.
Then I book tickets through an app, which is way more convenient than queuing at the box office.
I try to arrive about 20 to 30 minutes early so there's time to get snacks without rushing.
The cinema experience itself is special — the big screen, surround sound, and the shared atmosphere with other viewers is something you really can't replicate at home.
After the movie, if I'm with friends we always dissect it over drinks or dessert somewhere nearby.
If watched alone, I'll read reviews online and compare perspectives.

A.vi: Nam diễn viên được yêu thích nhất
cau: My favorite actor is Tom Hanks.
I've admired him for years because of his incredible range and authenticity.
What impresses me most is that he makes you believe every single role — whether it's Cast Away, Forrest Gump, or The Da Vinci Code.
He never seems to be 'performing' — it just feels completely genuine.
I also deeply respect him as a person.
From everything I've read, he's known as one of the kindest and most humble people in Hollywood.
Among Korean actors, I really admire Song Kang-ho, who starred in Parasite.
His ability to play morally complex characters is remarkable.
Good acting, to me, is about making the audience forget they're watching a film — and both of these actors achieve that effortlessly.

A.vi: Tả chuyến du lịch trong nước
cau: One of my most memorable domestic trips was to Da Nang with three close friends about two years ago.
We stayed for four days and three nights, which felt like just the right amount.
We checked out the Marble Mountains, My Khe Beach, the Dragon Bridge, and Ba Na Hills.
The highlight for me was spending a full day at the beach — swimming in the morning and just relaxing under the sun in the afternoon.
The seafood was outstanding.
We found this small local restaurant near the beach with incredibly fresh grilled fish and shrimp at really affordable prices.
One funny memory was getting lost on the way there and stumbling upon a lively local night market by accident.
We ended up spending an hour browsing — one of those unplanned moments that turns out to be the best part of the trip.
I'd love to go back someday.

A.vi: Miêu tả điểm du lịch (ở đâu, làm gì, với ai)
cau: I'd like to describe a trip to Hoi An — a charming ancient town in central Vietnam.
I went with two university friends and we spent three days exploring.
Hoi An is famous for its well-preserved old quarter, lantern-lit streets, and traditional crafts.
During the day we wandered through the old town, had some custom clothes made at a tailor, and rented bicycles to explore the rice paddies and nearby beaches.
At night, the town transforms into something magical — streets glowing with colorful lanterns reflected in the river.
We had dinner at a traditional restaurant overlooking the water and I still remember how peaceful it was.
What made the trip special wasn't just the scenery but the pace.
Hoi An felt like stepping back in time, and it reminded me how valuable it is to slow down sometimes.

A.vi: Miêu tả một quốc gia bạn đã đi nghỉ ở nước ngoài
cau: I had the chance to visit South Korea for a short work trip, and I made the most of my days off to do some sightseeing.
I visited Seoul, and I was immediately struck by how clean, organized, and efficient the city is.
The metro system was incredibly convenient — easy to navigate even without knowing much Korean.
I visited Gyeongbokgung Palace, which was stunning — traditional Korean architecture surrounded by modern skyscrapers.
I also explored Insadong for traditional crafts and Myeongdong for street food and shopping.
The food was a real highlight — bibimbap, Korean BBQ, tteokbokki... all delicious.
What impressed me most was how ancient culture and cutting-edge technology coexist so seamlessly.
It was a short visit, but it left a strong impression.
I'd love to go back for a proper holiday.

A.vi: Lý do mọi người thích đi du lịch? Lý do nào quan trọng nhất?
cau: I think people travel for all sorts of reasons, and each one is completely valid.
Some people travel to relax and escape the stress of daily life — just getting away from familiar surroundings can be incredibly refreshing.
Others go to experience new cultures, food, and perspectives.
And many people travel for adventure — hiking, diving, exploring landscapes they've never seen.
And of course, some travel specifically to spend quality time with family or friends and create shared memories.
If I had to pick the most important reason... I'd say gaining new perspectives.
Travel forces you out of your comfort zone and shows you there are many different, equally valid ways of living.
That kind of experience makes you more empathetic, open-minded, and genuinely grateful for your own life.

A.vi: Kỷ niệm về chuyến du lịch đáng nhớ
cau: The most memorable travel experience I've had was a solo trip to Sapa in northern Vietnam.
It was my first time traveling completely alone, which felt both exciting and a little daunting, to be honest.
I took an overnight train from Hanoi and arrived in the early morning surrounded by misty mountains and rice terraces.
It was breathtaking.
I joined a local trekking group and spent two days hiking through villages of ethnic minority communities.
One moment that really stood out — a local family invited me into their home for tea.
We couldn't really communicate because of the language barrier, but the warmth and hospitality they showed me was genuinely touching.
That experience taught me that human connection doesn't always need words — kindness is universal.
It remains one of the most meaningful trips I've ever taken.

A.vi: Những thứ cần chuẩn bị khi đi du lịch
cau: I like to plan carefully, but without over-scheduling everything.
The first thing I do is research the destination — must-see places, local food, weather, transport options.
Then I book accommodation and transport in advance, especially if it's peak season.
For packing, I have a checklist: weather-appropriate clothes, toiletries, medication, a basic first-aid kit, and copies of important documents.
I always bring a portable power bank since I rely heavily on my phone for navigation, translation, and photos.
I also download offline maps and save key addresses in case I lose internet connection.
A bit of local cash is always useful, and I make sure to share my itinerary with a family member so someone knows where I am.
Good preparation really does let you relax and enjoy the trip.

A.vi: Miêu tả nơi muốn du lịch và đưa lời khuyên cho Jiwon
cau: A place I've always wanted to visit is Japan — specifically Kyoto during cherry blossom season.
I'm drawn to Japan because of its perfect blend of ancient tradition and modern innovation.
Kyoto appeals to me for its temples, tea houses, bamboo groves, and peaceful gardens.
I imagine walking through the Arashiyama bamboo forest in the early morning, before the crowds arrive, would be extraordinary.
If I were advising my Korean colleague Jiwon on visiting Vietnam, I'd say: start with Hoi An.
It's beautiful, walkable, and gives you a completely different side of Vietnam from the busy cities.
Go early in the morning to explore the old town before the heat kicks in.
And don't miss Cao Lau — a local noodle dish that's only made properly in Hoi An.
Absolutely delicious.
Best time to visit is February to April, when the weather is dry and pleasant.

A.vi: Miêu tả công viên / chuyện đáng nhớ khi đi công viên
cau: There's a public park not far from my apartment that I visit regularly, mainly for morning jogs.
It's a medium-sized park built around a lake with a jogging path, benches, and shaded areas under tall trees.
In the mornings, it's full of life — elderly residents doing tai chi, families with young kids.
I usually go around 6 AM for a 30 to 40-minute jog before work.
One memorable incident happened a few months ago.
I was jogging while listening to music, admiring the lake view, when I tripped on an uneven patch of pavement and fell.
Knee scraped, earphones flying — pretty embarrassing, especially since people nearby saw it happen.
Fortunately, a kind woman nearby came over and offered me a wet wipe and asked if I was okay.
That small act of kindness really made me feel better.
Since then, I definitely pay more attention to where I'm running.

A.vi: Công viên: đi hồi bé với ai, làm gì, so sánh 2 công viên, việc bảo tồn
cau: When I was young, my parents used to take me to a big public park near our home every Sunday morning — a real family ritual.
My brother and I would run around, kick a ball, and feed the ducks by the pond while my parents walked and chatted.
Happy memories.
Compared to the park I use now in Hanoi, the one from my childhood was much larger and felt more natural — more trees, more open grass, less urban.
My current park is well-maintained but more of an urban recreational space.
As for conservation — I think it's extremely important, especially in fast-growing cities like Hanoi.
Parks provide essential green space, cleaner air, and real mental health benefits.
I genuinely think the city should invest more in expanding and maintaining them, rather than converting green areas into commercial developments.

A.vi: Ở nước bạn chủ yếu dùng phương tiện gì?
cau: In Vietnam, the most widely used form of transport is definitely the motorbike.
Almost every household owns at least one — it's affordable, cheap to run, and perfect for navigating narrow streets and heavy traffic.
In Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, you can see thousands of motorbikes on the road at any given time.
Public buses exist and are fairly cheap, but the routes aren't always convenient, so not everyone relies on them.
Ride-hailing apps like Grab have become huge in recent years — offering both motorbike and car options.
I personally commute by motorbike most days since my office is only about 15 minutes away.
And Hanoi's metro recently opened a new line, which is a really positive development for reducing congestion.

A.vi: So sánh phương tiện giao thông ngày xưa và bây giờ
cau: Transportation in Vietnam has changed dramatically over the past two or three decades.
When my parents were young, bicycles were the primary way of getting around — to school, to the market, to work.
Slow, but practical and eco-friendly.
Then as the economy grew rapidly in the 90s and 2000s, motorbikes became affordable for most households and quickly replaced bicycles.
Today, the streets are dominated by motorbikes, with a growing number of private cars as well.
Ride-hailing apps and GPS navigation have also made commuting much more convenient.
The downside is severe traffic congestion and air pollution in major cities.
I think the future needs to prioritize public transport, cycling infrastructure, and electric vehicles to make cities more sustainable.

A.vi: Vấn đề gặp phải với phương tiện giao thông và cách giải quyết
cau: The most common problem I face is traffic congestion during rush hours.
My commute normally takes 15 minutes, but during peak hours — around 7:30 to 8:30 AM — it can stretch to 40 minutes or more.
That's both time-consuming and stressful, especially with an early morning meeting.
My solution is to leave home earlier, around 7 AM, to avoid the worst of it.
Another issue is unexpected rain while riding without a raincoat.
I now always keep a compact foldable raincoat in my bag during the rainy season.
I once had a flat tyre on the way to work too, which was stressful because I wasn't near a repair shop.
Luckily a nearby resident pointed me to one just two streets away.
That experience taught me to have repair shop locations saved on my phone — just in case.

A.vi: Ký ức không tốt liên quan tới phương tiện giao thông
cau: One unpleasant memory happened about a year ago in the summer.
I was riding home from work when I got caught in a sudden, very heavy rainstorm.
I hadn't checked the forecast, and I had no raincoat with me.
The rain was so intense the road flooded in several places and visibility was really poor.
I had to pull over under a small overhang and wait for about 45 minutes, completely soaked.
What made it worse was that my phone battery died, so I couldn't call anyone or check a map.
By the time I got home, my clothes and shoes were completely waterlogged, and I ended up catching a cold the next day.
Genuinely miserable experience.
But I learned from it — now I always check the weather before heading out and carry a raincoat during the wet season.

A.vi: Thời tiết ở thành phố của bạn – so sánh với thành phố khác và quá khứ
cau: Hanoi has a four-season climate, which makes it quite different from Ho Chi Minh City in the south.
Ho Chi Minh City basically has two seasons — dry and rainy — and stays warm all year, around 25 to 35 degrees.
Hanoi, on the other hand, has proper winters that can drop to around 10 degrees, mild springs, hot summers, and cool autumns.
Personally, I love Hanoi's spring — the weather is mild, breezy, and really comfortable for outdoor activities.
Compared to the past, though, I feel the weather has become more extreme in recent years.
Summers seem longer and hotter, winters less predictable.
I think part of it is the urban heat island effect as the city expands, and part of it is broader climate change.
It's a concerning trend.

A.vi: Thời tiết ở nước bạn – so sánh với nước khác
cau: Vietnam has a tropical monsoon climate with significant regional variation.
The south has two seasons — dry from November to April, rainy from May to October.
The north, where I live, has four proper seasons.
Compared to countries like South Korea or Japan, Vietnam is significantly warmer on average.
When I visited Seoul for work, the winter temperatures were well below zero — nothing like what I experience in Hanoi.
In terms of rainfall, Vietnam gets a lot during monsoon season — heavy downpours that can cause localized flooding, especially in Hanoi.
The heat and humidity here in summer can feel pretty intense to visitors from more temperate countries.
But I do think the lush greenery and vibrant nature that comes with a tropical climate is one of Vietnam's great natural assets.

A.vi: Sự kiện đáng nhớ xảy ra do thời tiết, cách bạn giải quyết
cau: A weather event that stands out was a strong typhoon that hit Hanoi a few years ago.
The city issued warnings the night before, so I stocked up on food and water in advance.
The next morning the wind was incredibly strong and the rain relentless.
I decided to work from home.
But around midday, the power went out and stayed out for about six hours.
Without electricity I couldn't work or charge anything.
My laptop battery lasted about three hours, which I used for the most urgent tasks.
I ended up eating cold food and spending the afternoon reading a paperback by the window — honestly not the worst afternoon.
When the power came back, I charged everything immediately and made a note to buy a proper backup power bank.
The experience really highlighted how dependent we are on electricity in modern life.

A.vi: Thời tiết thay đổi những năm gần đây? Nguyên nhân và ảnh hưởng
cau: I've definitely noticed that weather patterns in Vietnam have become more unpredictable and extreme in recent years.
Summers in Hanoi are getting hotter — temperatures regularly exceed 40 degrees during peak months.
Even a short rainstorm can now cause significant flooding in parts of the city.
Winters, on the other hand, have become shorter and milder, disrupting the traditional seasonal rhythm.
think the main causes are global climate change driven by greenhouse gas emissions, combined with rapid urbanization that reduces green cover and amplifies the heat island effect.
The consequences are significant — crop failures, more severe flooding in coastal regions, and real health impacts from heat stress.
On a personal level, the increasingly hot summers are just uncomfortable — they affect how much time I can spend outdoors.
I think individuals, businesses, and governments all share responsibility to reduce emissions and adapt to these changes.

A.vi: Miêu tả máy tính của bạn
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: I use a gemini Galaxy Book laptop for both work and personal use — which feels pretty fitting given where I work.
It's a 15-inch Full HD display, bright and clear, which really matters when you're staring at code for hours.
It's also relatively lightweight with a slim profile, so I can carry it to meetings or cafes without any hassle.
It has a fast processor and enough RAM to run multiple development environments simultaneously without slowing down.
Battery life is decent — I can usually get through a full workday without needing to plug in.
Working in software development, having a reliable and powerful machine is essential, and this one meets my needs well.

A.vi: Miêu tả máy tính (màn hình, âm thanh)
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: The screen is a 15-inch Full HD display with good color accuracy and brightness — comfortable to work on for extended periods.
At my office desk, I've connected an external 24-inch monitor as well, for better ergonomics and more screen space.
That dual-screen setup makes development significantly more efficient — code on one screen, browser or documentation on the other.
As for audio, the built-in speakers are decent for video calls and casual music.
But for anything more serious — watching a film or actually enjoying music — I always use my wireless earphones.
Good audio quality matters to me because music is such a regular part of my routine.

A.vi: Miêu tả điện thoại di động
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: I'm currently using a gemini Galaxy S series smartphone — I've had it for about two years now.
The screen is a large, vibrant AMOLED display that makes everything look great, whether I'm reading or watching videos.
The camera is one of its strongest features.
I use it regularly when traveling or just out on walks, and the results are consistently impressive.
The phone handles multitasking really well, which matters since I switch between a lot of apps throughout the day.
Battery life is solid — comfortably lasts a full day with moderate to heavy use.
I use it for pretty much everything: work email, messaging, navigation, music, and mobile banking.
Working at gemini, I'm also genuinely interested in how these features evolve with each new generation.

A.vi: Tại sao bạn muốn mua một chiếc điện thoại mới?
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: My current phone has served me well for two years, but I've been thinking about upgrading for a few reasons.
First, the battery has started to degrade noticeably.
By the end of a busy day it often needs charging, whereas before it would easily last until bedtime.
Second, I'd love a better camera.
The newer gemini models have significantly improved sensors and computational photography features.
Third, storage is getting tight — two years of photos, apps, and files have accumulated and I'm constantly managing space.
And as a software engineer, using the latest device helps me stay current with the platform's capabilities.
I'm not in a rush, but within the next few months I'll probably make the switch to the latest gemini flagship.

A.vi: Đồ vật người Việt Nam dùng nhiều nhất
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: Without question, the object Vietnamese people use most in their daily lives is the mobile phone.
Vietnam has one of the highest smartphone penetration rates in Southeast Asia, and it's easy to see why.
People use their phones for virtually everything — calls, messaging, banking, shopping, navigation, entertainment, and food delivery.
Apps like Zalo for messaging, Grab for transport and delivery, and various banking apps have become essential daily tools.
Mobile payment is growing rapidly too — many people now pay for groceries, coffee, even street food using QR codes.
For younger generations especially, the smartphone is the central device for both work and social life.
It's genuinely hard to imagine daily life in Vietnam without one now.

A.vi: Điện thoại di động quá khứ và hiện tại
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: My relationship with phones has changed dramatically over the years.
My first phone, when I was about 15, was a basic Nokia feature phone.
It could make calls, send texts, and play Snake — that was pretty much it.
The screen was tiny and black and white, but I was genuinely thrilled to have it.
When I started university, I got my first touchscreen smartphone.
The difference was incredible — suddenly I had internet, apps, maps, and a camera in my pocket.
I still remember the first time I used Google Maps to navigate somewhere unfamiliar.
It felt almost magical.
My current gemini Galaxy is a world away from that old Nokia.
The processing power alone would have seemed like science fiction to my teenage self.
The evolution in just one generation is genuinely remarkable.

A.vi: Kinh nghiệm đáng nhớ khi dùng điện thoại
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: One really memorable experience happened about a year and a half ago.
I was jogging near my apartment when I slipped on a wet surface and dropped my phone into a shallow puddle.
The screen went black almost immediately.
I panicked.
I dried it off, tried turning it on — nothing.
I searched online and found the classic advice about putting it in uncooked rice to absorb the moisture.
I left it overnight, and by the next morning it turned back on.
I was genuinely relieved — and a little amazed, honestly.
The screen glitched for a few days but eventually returned to normal.
After that I immediately bought a waterproof case and a screen protector.
It taught me how fragile and valuable these devices really are.

A.vi: Vấn đề với điện thoại (hỏng/sự cố), cách bạn giải quyết
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: The most serious phone issue I've faced was when my previous smartphone suddenly stopped charging after about 18 months of use.
I tried different cables and adaptors — nothing worked.
The battery was draining and there was no way to charge it.
Since it was still under warranty, I took it to the official gemini service center.
After running diagnostics, they found the charging port was faulty due to a manufacturing defect.
They replaced it free of charge under warranty, which took about a week.
During that week without my phone, I borrowed an old spare from my brother to stay reachable.
It was inconvenient, but it reminded me how much I rely on my smartphone for everyday tasks.
Now I make a habit of backing up data to cloud storage regularly — just in case.

A.vi: Internet quá khứ và hiện tại; kinh nghiệm dùng Facebook đáng nhớ
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: Internet usage in Vietnam has changed beyond recognition over the past 15 years.
When I was in middle school, internet meant going to a PC café and paying by the hour for slow connections.
Websites took ages to load, streaming video was basically impossible.
Now I have fast 4G and 5G on my phone and fiber optic broadband at home.
I can stream 4K video, join video calls, and upload large files with no issues at all.
As for a memorable Facebook experience — a few years ago, an old school friend I hadn't spoken to in about eight years sent me a message out of nowhere.
He'd seen some photos I'd posted and reached out.
We ended up meeting for coffee and catching up on everything.
That reconnection was one of the most pleasant surprises social media has given me.
We've stayed in touch regularly ever since.

A.vi: So sánh Internet hiện tại và quá khứ
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: The contrast between internet use now and 10 to 15 years ago is pretty extraordinary.
In the past, access in Vietnam was slow, expensive, and mostly limited to PC cafés or schools.
People used it mainly for basic browsing, email, or chatting on Yahoo Messenger.
Accessing news took time, and streaming anything was practically impossible.
Today, high-speed internet is widely available, affordable, and accessible on any smartphone, pretty much anywhere in the country.
Video calling family in perfect quality, streaming any film instantly, working remotely without technical limitations — all normal now.
The downsides are information overload, privacy concerns, and addictive usage patterns.
But on balance, the improvements to daily life and economic opportunity have been enormously positive.

A.vi: Giới thiệu về SNS (mạng xã hội), SNS hay dùng và những mặt tiêu cực
topic_src: CÔNG NGHỆ (INTERNET, ĐIỆN THOẠI, MÁY TÍNH)
cau: Social networking services have become a really integral part of modern life in Vietnam.
The most popular platforms here are Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, and Zalo — which is a local messaging and social app.
personally use Facebook to stay connected with friends and family, and scroll through Instagram occasionally for photography and tech content.
SNS has genuine benefits — maintaining relationships across distances, staying informed, even growing small businesses.
But the negatives are significant and shouldn't be ignored.
The most serious problem is misinformation.
False news spreads faster than corrections, and many people believe things without verifying them.
Cyberbullying is another major concern, especially for young people.
Excessive social media use has also been linked to anxiety and lower self-esteem.
Personally, I try to limit my daily usage and be selective about what I engage with.

A.vi: Làm gì vào ngày nghỉ?
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: On my days off, I try to balance rest, personal development, and seeing people.
usually wake up a bit later than usual — around 7:30 — and start with a morning jog at the nearby park.
After that and a good breakfast, I might work on personal coding projects or catch up on tech articles.
In the afternoon, I'll often meet friends for lunch or coffee, or go explore a new part of the city.
I really enjoy discovering new cafes and restaurants — Hanoi has a fantastic food scene that I feel I've barely scratched the surface of.
In the evenings, I usually wind down with a movie or a few episodes of something.
Sometimes on weekends I'll take a short day trip to the countryside or a lake outside the city.
A good day off leaves me feeling genuinely recharged for the week ahead.

A.vi: Kỷ niệm về ngày nghỉ đặc biệt
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: One day off that stands out was last year on my birthday.
My friends organized a surprise picnic at a lakeside park outside Hanoi — without telling me anything in advance.
I thought we were just going for a casual drive.
When we arrived, there were blankets, food, a cake, and a little Bluetooth speaker already set up.
We spent the whole afternoon eating, listening to music, playing games, and watching the sunset over the lake.
It was such a simple setting, but the laughter and warmth of being surrounded by people who genuinely care... it felt extraordinary.
No fancy restaurant or expensive gift could have matched that feeling.
The best memories really do come from genuine effort and thoughtfulness, not grand gestures.

A.vi: Chạy bộ với ai, làm gì trước/sau khi chạy, tại sao thích chạy bộ?
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: I usually jog by myself, which I actually prefer — it gives me quiet time to think and decompress.
Before going, I always drink a glass of water and do about 5 minutes of dynamic stretching to warm up.
I run for 30 to 40 minutes, usually around the lake in the park near my apartment.
After finishing, I walk slowly to cool down, then go home to shower and have breakfast.
I started jogging about two years ago when I realized I was sitting at a desk for 8+ hours a day and not getting nearly enough physical activity.
What I love most is the mental clarity it brings.
After a good run, my mind feels calm and organized — which is really invaluable before a full workday.
It's become a habit that helps me feel structured and disciplined overall.

A.vi: Chuyện gọi điện cho bạn: nói gì, khi nào, bao lâu một lần
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: I catch up with close friends on the phone about once or twice a week, depending on how busy everyone is.
Usually I call to check in and chat — how work's going, anything funny or interesting that happened, or to make plans to meet up.
Sometimes it's to ask for advice on something specific — a work decision, a purchase, a personal situation.
Calls typically last 15 to 30 minutes, unless we get into a really engaging topic, in which case it can go on much longer.
I prefer voice calls over text for proper conversations — you can convey tone and emotion so much more naturally.
I also regularly video call my parents, who live in another city.
At least once a week — it really helps me feel connected even though I'm far from home.

A.vi: Tình huống không nghe được điện thoại
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: There have been a few times I missed calls and it caused some inconvenience.
The most memorable was when my phone was on silent during an important work meeting.
My mother had been trying to reach me for about two hours — she wasn't feeling well and wanted some reassurance.
When I finally finished and checked my phone, there were five missed calls.
I immediately felt terrible.
I called her back right away, and thankfully it wasn't a serious emergency — just a headache and some anxiety.
But the guilt of having been unreachable stayed with me for the rest of the day.
Since then I've made a habit of checking missed calls immediately after any meeting.
And I let my family know in advance when I'll be unavailable for a while, so they don't worry.

A.vi: Giới thiệu về ngân hàng gần nhà / ấn tượng về ngân hàng nào nhất
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: The bank I use most is Vietcombank — there's a branch about 10 minutes from my apartment.
It's a fairly modern branch with a comfortable waiting area and a well-organized queuing system.
I've visited a few times for things like account updates or processing a larger transfer that needed in- person verification.
The staff have been professional and helpful every time.
But honestly, what impresses me most is their mobile banking app.
It's fast, secure, and covers almost every transaction I need — transfers, bill payments, card management.
Since I started using it, I rarely need to visit the branch at all.
The combination of reliable in-person service and a great digital platform is what makes Vietcombank stand out for me.

A.vi: Bị vấn đề gì nên vào bệnh viện? Ký ức về việc đó / Ai giới thiệu?
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: About two years ago, I had to visit the hospital due to persistent stomach pain that lasted for several days.
At first I figured it was something minor — bad food, maybe — so I rested and drank plenty of water.
But when the pain got worse and started affecting my sleep, a colleague really encouraged me to get checked properly.
She recommended Dr. Hung at Viet Duc Hospital, saying he'd helped her with something similar before.
I went the next morning.
After an examination and some tests, Dr. Hung diagnosed a mild gastric inflammation, likely from stress and irregular eating habits.
He prescribed medication and dietary adjustments for three weeks.
What stood out was his patience — he explained everything clearly and answered all my questions without making me feel rushed.
The treatment worked well, and that experience taught me to take my eating habits more seriously and not delay seeking medical help.

A.vi: Bệnh viện: tại sao đi hồi bé, ký ức vui vẻ với bác sĩ tốt bụng
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: When I was young, I visited the hospital mainly for respiratory infections and fever — pretty standard childhood stuff.
One visit when I was about 8 stands out as a positive memory.
I had a high fever and was quite scared.
But the pediatrician who treated me was a wonderfully warm woman.
She spoke to me gently, explained every step of the examination in child-friendly language so I wouldn't be frightened.
She even gave me a small sticker at the end, which absolutely delighted me at that age.
I remember telling my mum on the way home that I wanted to be a doctor when I grew up — purely because of how kind that doctor had been.
That experience left me with a genuinely positive impression of the medical profession.
It taught me early on that the best healthcare isn't just about technical skill — the human side of medicine matters enormously.

A.vi: Lần đầu đi cắt tóc: khi nào, với ai, cảm giác như thế nào?
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: My first independent haircut was when I was about 17, the summer before starting university.
Until then, my mother had always come with me to the barber and handled the communication.
This time I decided to go alone and manage it myself.
I walked into a small barbershop near our house and tried to explain what I wanted — shorter on the sides, some length on top.
Unfortunately, I was too vague and a bit nervous, so the barber made his own interpretation.
When I looked in the mirror... the result was much shorter than I'd imagined.
My eyes went wide.
I didn't say anything because I felt too awkward, paid, and left.
My friends and family teased me about it for weeks.
Looking back, it was a small but important lesson: communicate clearly and specifically — and don't be afraid to speak up.

A.vi: Kỷ niệm không tốt liên quan đến cắt tóc và cách xử lý
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: A more recent bad haircut experience happened about two years ago at a new barbershop I was trying for the first time.
I showed the barber a reference photo and explained clearly what I wanted.
He nodded confidently and said he could do it.
The end result looked nothing like the photo.
The sides were uneven and the top was way shorter than I'd asked for.
I was genuinely unhappy with it.
But this time — unlike my teenage self — I decided to say something politely.
I told him it wasn't quite what I'd hoped for and asked if he could make some adjustments to even it out.
He apologized and tried to fix it, though the damage was mostly done at that point.
I paid, left, and resolved not to go back.
The lesson: even with a clear photo, only go to a barber who comes recommended or whose work you've seen before.

A.vi: Các loại giấy tờ tùy thân ở quốc gia bạn
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: In Vietnam, the primary ID is the CCCD — the Citizen Identification Card — which replaced the old system a few years ago.
Every citizen aged 14 and above is required to have one.
It contains your name, date of birth, address, nationality, and a unique 12-digit ID number.
It's also embedded with a chip storing biometric data, making it more secure than older ID systems.
You need it in almost every official situation — opening a bank account, signing contracts, booking flights, registering a SIM card, applying for jobs.
To get one, you go to your local police station with supporting documents.
They take a photo and fingerprints, and the card is usually issued within 7 to 14 days.
If it's damaged or has incorrect information, you return to the police station and apply for a replacement.
The process is straightforward, so it's important to store the card safely and report errors immediately.

A.vi: Đồ gia dụng gặp vấn đề và cách xử lý
topic_src: HOẠT ĐỘNG THƯỜNG NGÀY & DỊCH VỤ
cau: The most disruptive appliance issue I've had was when my refrigerator stopped cooling properly.
I noticed one morning when my food was no longer cold and the milk had gone off overnight.
I checked the basics first — making sure it was plugged in properly, checking the thermostat settings.
That didn't help.
So I looked up the brand's customer service number online and called to describe the problem.
They scheduled a technician for the following afternoon.
The technician found a faulty compressor and said it would take three to four days to repair.
During that time I stored perishables in a cooler with ice and kept grocery shopping to daily essentials.
After the repair, the fridge worked perfectly.
And importantly, it was still under warranty — so the repair was covered.
That reminded me to always check warranty status before agreeing to pay for repairs.

A.vi: Chuyến du lịch có vấn đề – gọi điện cho đại lý đổi lịch
cau: Hi, this is Son calling.
I booked a two-day trip to Da Nang through your agency last week — it was scheduled for this Saturday the 10th.
Something unexpected has come up at work, so unfortunately I won't be able to travel on that date.
Is there any chance I could reschedule to the following Saturday, the 17th?
Could you also check whether the hotel and transport arrangements can be moved to the new date as well?
If there are any rescheduling fees, just let me know the amount and how I can take care of it.
I'd really appreciate your help.
Could you give me a call back once you've confirmed availability?
Thank you so much.

A.vi: Giúp đỡ người nước ngoài bị lạc đường
cau: Excuse me — are you lost?
Can I help?
Oh, you're looking for Hoan Kiem Lake!
No worries at all — it's not far from here.
Just head straight down this street for about 200 meters, then turn left at the big intersection.
You'll see a red pedestrian bridge — the lake is just past that, on your right.
Should take about 10 minutes on foot.
If you have Google Maps open, I can show you exactly on your screen.
No problem at all!
Welcome to Hanoi — I hope you have a great visit!

A.vi: Mua giày tập bị bất tiện – đến cửa hàng giải thích
cau: Hello, I bought a pair of running shoes here about a week ago and I've run into a problem with them.
The sole on the left shoe has started coming apart at the front edge — and I've only worn them three or four times for light jogging.
I have the receipt and the shoes are still in the original box.
I believe this is a manufacturing defect, not damage from use — I've been wearing them completely normally.
I'd like to either exchange them for a new pair of the same model and size, or get a refund if that model's no longer available.
Could you help me with this?
I'd really appreciate a quick resolution — thank you.

A.vi: Mất đồ trên taxi – gọi điện tới công ty taxi
cau: Hello, I'd like to report a lost item.
I took one of your taxis about an hour ago.
I traveled from Dinh Tien Hoang Street in Hoan Kiem District to Galaxy Building in Cau Giay District.
When I got home, I realized I'd left my laptop bag on the back seat.
It's a black bag with a grey strap, and it contains my work laptop and some important documents.
I have the receipt with me — it was taxi number 58K-12345 at around 5:40 PM.
Could you please check with the driver?
I'll come to collect it immediately if it's been found.
Please contact me at this number — thank you so much, I really appreciate your help.

A.vi: Ở khách sạn lâu ngày – hỏi lễ tân về chỗ vui chơi gần đó
cau: Good afternoon!
I've been staying here for three days now and I have a free afternoon today.
Could you recommend some interesting things to do or places to visit nearby?
I'm especially interested in local food — are there any well-known street food areas or traditional restaurants within walking distance?
I'd also love to see some cultural or historical sites if there are any close by.
And is there anywhere I could rent a bicycle?
I'd love to cycle around and explore.
If possible, could you write down the names of the places for me?
My Vietnamese reading isn't very strong, so having it written out would be really helpful.
Thank you so much!

A.vi: Hỏi Ava (máy tính) về nơi ở của nó
cau: Hey Ava!
I have a fun question for you today — where do you actually live, or where are you located?
Do you have a physical home somewhere, or do you exist entirely in digital space?
As a software engineer, I find it genuinely interesting to think about where AI systems actually run.
Are you hosted on dedicated servers, or distributed across cloud infrastructure in multiple data centers around the world?
And does the concept of 'home' mean anything to you, or is location completely irrelevant from your perspective?
I'm really curious to hear your answer — or your best attempt at one!

A.vi: Gọi điện cho bạn hỏi cách sử dụng máy MP3
cau: Hey Minh, it's Son!
Sorry to bother you — do you have a few minutes?
So I just borrowed an MP3 player and I'm having trouble figuring it out.
How do I skip between songs?
Every time I press the button it just goes to a menu instead of the next track.
And how do I adjust the volume?
I pressed what looked like the volume buttons but the track changed instead.
Oh, and is there a way to create a playlist, or does it just play everything in order?
I know it sounds basic but I genuinely haven't used one of these in years!
Thanks so much — I really appreciate it.

A.vi: Mượn máy MP3 nhưng làm hỏng – giải thích và đưa ra phương án giải quyết
cau: Hey Minh, I need to talk to you about something — and I want to apologize in advance.
I accidentally dropped your MP3 player earlier today while I was jogging, and the screen cracked.
I feel really terrible about it — I should have been more careful with something I borrowed.
I completely take responsibility, and I want to make it right.
I'd like to pay for the screen repair, or if that's not practical, I'll replace it with a new equivalent model — whichever works better for you.
Could you check how much a repair would cost?
Or if you'd prefer a replacement, just let me know what you'd want.
Again, I'm really sorry — please don't hesitate to tell me how you'd like to handle it.

A.vi: Điện thoại mới mua bị lỗi – yêu cầu 2 giải pháp từ đại lý
cau: Hello, I purchased a new smartphone from your store three days ago, and I've already run into a significant problem.
When I make calls, the person on the other end can barely hear me.
The microphone doesn't seem to be functioning properly.
I haven't dropped the phone or exposed it to water — the issue appeared from the very first day of use.
I have the receipt and original packaging here with me.
I'd like to request two possible solutions.
First, could you replace this unit with a brand-new one of the same model?
Alternatively, if that's not possible, could the phone be sent for warranty repair, with a temporary device provided in the meantime?
This is my primary work phone, so I'd really appreciate a quick resolution.
Thank you for your help.

A.vi: Mua nhầm áo – gọi điện giải quyết; nhờ chủ cửa hàng tư vấn
cau: Hello, I bought a shirt from your store yesterday but when I got home I realized I'd accidentally picked up a large instead of a medium.
The shirt still has all its tags on and hasn't been worn.
Would it be possible to exchange it for the correct size?
Also, while I have you on the line — I was hoping you could give me some advice.
I'm looking for a versatile casual shirt — smart enough for the office but comfortable for weekends too.
Do you have any new arrivals that might fit that description, preferably in neutral colors?
I'll bring the original shirt and receipt when I come in.
Would this afternoon work?
Thanks so much for your help!

A.vi: Cửa sổ hỏng – gọi người sửa; gọi lại khi mãi không thấy tới
cau: (Call 1 – Báo sự cố)
Hello, I'm calling to report a problem in my apartment — I'm in unit 812, Building A.
One of my bedroom windows is broken — the latch is completely stuck and I can't close it properly.
Could you arrange for a technician to come and fix it?
Rain is expected this afternoon and leaving it open could cause water damage.
Would it be possible to have someone come this morning?
(Call 2 – Follow-up)
Hello again, this is Son from unit 812.
I called this morning about the broken window and was told a technician would arrive by 2 PM.
It's now 3:30 and no one has come yet.
Could you check on the status of my request?
It's become quite urgent — it's already started raining and water is coming in through the gap.
Could you either send someone in the next 30 minutes, or at least let me know when to expect them?
I'll be available for the rest of the afternoon.
Thank you.

A.vi: Đi làm giấy tờ tùy thân mới gặp vấn đề / giấy tờ bị sai thông tin
cau: (Báo lỗi)
Good morning.
I came here last month to apply for a new CCCD and I've recently received the card.
However, I noticed that my date of birth is printed incorrectly.
It shows the 15th, but the correct date is the 5th.
I have my old ID card and household registration book here to verify the correct information.
Could you please help me process a correction and reissue the card?
(Yêu cầu xử lý nhanh)
I understand this may take some time, but I have an important banking appointment next week that requires a valid ID.
Is there any way to expedite the correction, given that the error was on your end?
I'll cooperate with whatever documentation you need.
I really appreciate your help.

A.vi: Đến tiệm bảo cắt tóc / cắt không ưng, yêu cầu cắt lại
cau: (Yêu cầu kiểu tóc)
Hi!
I'd like a haircut please.
I'd like to keep the top at around 5 centimeters — not too short — with the sides faded on a number two.
The front should be styled slightly forward, not too pushed back.
Here's a photo on my phone that shows roughly what I'm going for.
Take your time — I'm not in a hurry at all.
(Sau khi cắt – yêu cầu điều chỉnh)
Thank you!
I really like the overall shape, but I feel the top came out a little shorter than I was hoping for.
Would it be possible to blend the sides a bit more so the transition is a bit smoother?
I know the length can't be added back, but I think a cleaner fade would really improve it.
Thanks for your patience — and I'll make sure to bring a clearer reference photo next time!

A.vi: Công ty du lịch báo lỗi phòng – gọi điện trao đổi với bố mẹ đổi hành trình
cau: Mum, Dad — I just got off the phone with the travel agency and there's a small issue we need to sort out.
It turns out the hotel room they booked for us in Hue has had a double-booking problem, so our rooms won't be available on the original dates.
The agency has given us two options.
We can either shift the whole trip by three days to the week after, or they can arrange a different hotel of similar quality in the same city.
Personally, I think the second option is simpler — we wouldn't need to rebook our transport.
But if you'd prefer to push the dates back entirely, I can check whether we can get the time off work.
What do you think?
The agency needs an answer by tomorrow so they can finalize everything — just let me know your preference and I'll call them back right away.

A.vi: Mua đồ bị hỏng sau khi giặt – gọi điện phàn nàn / đòi bồi thường
cau: Hello, I'm calling to report a problem with a shirt I bought at your store last week.
I followed the washing instructions on the label exactly — cold water, gentle cycle, air dry.
But after washing it just once, the color has faded dramatically and the fabric seems to have weakened — there are small pulls in the threads.
I believe this is a quality defect with the garment itself, since I followed all the care instructions properly.
I still have the receipt and the shirt as evidence.
I'd like to request either a full refund or a replacement of equivalent value.
Could you let me know your returns procedure for defective items?
Thank you.

A.vi: Kể về chuyến thăm một gia đình người bạn nước ngoài
cau: I'd like to share a really memorable experience from when I visited my Korean colleague Jiwon's family home during a work trip to Seoul last year.
Jiwon very kindly invited me to have dinner at his parents' house, which I thought was a wonderful gesture.
When I arrived, his parents greeted me so warmly — even though they spoke very little English.
They'd prepared an elaborate traditional Korean dinner — galbi, japchae, all sorts of banchan side dishes, and of course kimchi.
I was a little nervous about the dining etiquette, but Jiwon guided me gently and made sure I felt comfortable the whole time.
What touched me most was the effort his family put into making a foreign guest feel genuinely welcome.
Despite the language barrier, the warmth communicated everything.
It was a humbling and heartwarming experience — a real reminder of how much we share across cultures when we approach each other with kindness.

B.en: You indicated in the survey that you listen to music. What kind of music do you listen to? Who are some of your favorite musicians or composers?
cau: I like listening to pop music, because it has catchy melodies, the lyrics are easy to understand, and the sound is smooth and attractive.
My favorite singer is Selena Gomez.
She is also a famous songwriter, and actress.
Many songs she has written have become viral trends on the Internet and YouTube.
She is also remarkable beautiful, and her dancing is very nice.
Among her songs, I like Love You Like a Love Song the most.
It is also one of her most famous songs.
I was attracted by the story in this song, and I listen to it many times each day.

B.en: When and where do you usually go to listen to music? Do you listen to the radio? Do you go to concerts? Tell me about the different ways you enjoy music.
cau: I don't go to concerts.
Most of the time, I listen to music on my cell phone, so I can enjoy it wherever I am.
I usually listen to music in the car when I'm driving, or when I'm walking down the street.
Sometimes, I also listen to music while cooking or cleaning my house.
Even when I'm bored, I listen to music because it helps improve my mood and reduce stress very effectively.

B.en: When did you first become interested in music? What kinds of music did you like at first? Tell me how your interested in music developed from your childhood until today?
cau: I don't remember exactly, but in my mind, I love music from when I was a kid.
At that time we were poor, I didn't have opportunity to listen many kind of music.
I just listened to traditional music on the old radio of my family and the song that my mom, my grandmother sang.
Now, life become better, I can approach and listen to many kind of music.
Some time I listen to pop music, but some time I listen to rock music, or country music, Some time I listen to EDM music when I do exercise.
In conclusion, I listen to many types of music now.

B.en: Can you tell me about a memorable experience with music?
cau: Yes, I remember one special time when I went to a live concert of my favorite singer.
It was about three years ago.
The concert was held in a big stadium, and there were so many fans.
When the singer came on stage, everyone was screaming and singing along.
I felt so excited and happy because it is the first time that I saw my idol in real life.
That night was unforgettable, and it made me love music even more.

B.en: What kind of movies do you like to watch? Why do you like those type of movies?
cau: I watch many types of movies and TV programs, but my favorite types are action movies and nature documentaries.
Action movies are very interesting and help me to reduce stress very effectively
I also love nature, I love trees, flowers, and animals.
I want to know how beautiful wildlife is, and I want to understand how animals grow up and survive in the wild.
All of this attracts me a lot.

B.en: Who is your favorite actor or actress? Why do you like them?
cau: My favorite actor is Leonardo DiCaprio.
I first saw him in the movie Titanic, and his acting was amazing.
He is very talented and can play many different kinds of roles.
I also like that he helps poor children have opportunity to go to school and cares about the environment.
Whenever I watch his movies, I always feel very interested and enjoy them a lot.

B.en: Tell me about when you went to the movies recently. Who did you go with and how was that day? What did you do before the movie and what did you after?
cau: Last weekend was my friend's birthday.
We celebrated a surprise birthday to her, we drove to the cinema to watch an action movie.
Before the movie, we bought some popcorn and soft drinks like Coca-Cola and orange juice.
After the movie, we went to a nearby fast-food restaurant and ordered dried chicken with some snacks.
We were very hungry, and the food was so good — it was a very delicious meal.
Moreover, after the meal, We got one ice cream each.
We were full after all.
It was a nice and memorable day for me.

B.en: What was a memorable movie that you watched in the past? What was it about? What was special about that movie?
cau: The most memorable movie that I have seen is Titanic.
It is a romantic movie based on the true story of the famous Titanic ship.
The film has participation of my favourite actor also.
It tells the sensational love story between Jack and Rose, the two main characters, on a ship that sank on its first journey.
Even though the movie doesn't have a happy ending for the main characters.
But it took me a lot of tear during movie.
I still remember every scene and every line in the movie until now.

B.en: You indicated in the survey that you go to parks with adults. Tell me about the kinds of parks that you like to visit? What do the parks look like?
cau: There are a lot of parks around where I live, but there is one I like the most.
It's a large park with many big trees.
There is also a lake with a walking path around it.
I can feel the fresh air and spaceful when I am at there.
The park has a lot of sports facilities such as exercise bikes and pull-up bars.
Additionally, there are also many children playing around the park, with attractions like electric trains, slides and bubble house

B.en: Describe a typical visit to a park is like for you. Tell me about the things you do and see at parks?
cau: I usually go to the park to get some fresh air and do exercise.
Sometimes I go running, and sometimes I just take a walk alone or with a friend.
When I'm tired after a long day at work, I will go to the park and listen to music while running.
I see that most people go to the park for the same reason.
They do exercise and enjoy the fresh air.

B.en: Tell me about the last time you went to a park? Which park was it? When was it that you went? Tell me everything you did from the moment you arrived at the park to time you left.
cau: Last Sunday, my friends and I went to the park near my house.
We like going to the park a lot.
When we arrived, we walked around the lake and then played on the slide until we got tired.
After taking a rest and drinking some water, we played another favorite game: hide and seek.
When we became hungry and thirsty, we left the park and went to a nearby restaurant.
We ordered some food and drinks for the meal.
After that, we went home late and fell asleep right away after had a nice day.

B.en: Tell me about the last time you went to a park? Which park was it? When was it that you went? Tell me everything you did from the moment you arrived at the park to time you left.
cau: I remember going to a park with my family last month.
We had a small picnic and played some games together.
The weather was nice, and we enjoyed the fresh air and green trees.
However, something bad happened — it suddenly started to rain heavily.
We didn't bring any raincoats, so we all got wet and had to run to the car.
Even though it was a bit uncomfortable, we laughed a lot and it became a fun memory.

B.en: How did you first start going to parks? What made you visit parks in the first place? Why do you go to parks now?
cau: My purpose when I first went to the park was to get some fresh air.
At that time, I just enjoyed the trees and flowers there.
I usually sat on a bench and enjoyed the breeze.
But these days, I go to the park more frequently.
I go to the parks to get some exercise.
I can take a walk, ride a bicycle, or just do some simple exercise.
When I get tired after doing exercise, I can relax and enjoy the fresh air and open space of the park.
That is really great moments for me.

B.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel domestically. Tell me about some of the place you like to travel to and why you like going there?
cau: There're a of beautiful place in VietNam.
But there's one I think I like most, It is Ha Long Bay.
It is a Bay in the North of VietNam, I love there because I like walking along the shore, gazing at the sea and starry sky in the evening
And, Nature scenery there is very beautiful, there're thousand small islands in HaLong bay with different shape.
I stand on ship go around the island and look them beauty clearly.
Additionally, there're many kind of sea foods and price is quite cheap/affordable.
This is why I make it a point to visit Ha Long Bay every summer.

B.en: Can you tell me about the things you do in order to prepair to trips?.
cau: I'm a light packer, So when I travel.
I only bring essentials
Fistly, I pack a couple of clothers depending on the weather.
Then I add some basic emergency medicine.
I also bring a hat, a sunglasses and swim suit.
Of course ,I need toothbrush, toothpaste, and shampo for trip.
And I cannot forget bring my wallet and my phone and a charger.
That is all I need for my trip.

B.en: Tell me a bout one travel experience you had that was unforgettable. Start by telling me when this happended, where you were, and who you were with. Tell me about all the things that happended that make this experience so unforgettable?
cau: Last summer, during a company team-building trip, I had quite an unpleasant experience.
After lunch, I believe I ate something that was not fresh.
Soon after, my stomach started hurting, and I developed food poisoning.
I had a high fever and a severe headache throughout the afternoon.
I had to keep running to the bathroom due to diarrhea.
To improve my condition, I went to a pharmacy and got some medicine.
Fortunately, after taking the medicine, I started feeling better.
However, I had to stay in my room and rest the next day, missing out on all the activities during the trip.
Since then, I've learned to be much more cautious about what I eat, especially in unfamiliar situations.

B.en: Tell me about some of the trips that you took in your youth. Where did you go? Who did you go with? And what did you do or see during those early trips?
cau: When I was a kid, I often followed my parents going to the beach each summer.
We usually stayed at a beachside hotel with a great ocean view.
During the trip, we used to swim in the ocean.
We also played with ball and built sand castle.
Moreover, we also looked for seashell and crabs on the beach.
In the evening, we took a walk along the beach and listened to the sound of ocean.

B.en: You indicated in the survey that you travel internationally. Could you describe for me one of the countries you've visited? What did it look like? And what were the people like there?
cau: I went to Singapore last year.
It is a special trip because this is the first time I travel by plane.
Although It is small island country and large population, every where I saw is so clean and beautiful
People usually move by public transport or by foot so there is no traffic jam.
Food is delicious and price is expensive.
People are friendly and working hard.
That is so exciting expericence when I travel oversea.

B.en: Talk about the things that you typically do when you visit another country  or overseas city.
cau: When I visit another country , I try to visit the historic place there
I try to get expericence in street, go to special place at that country
I will try to taste local food.
Of course I will take picture to record the nice moment.
I also want to wear tradition clothes and take part in festival to understand more about the life and the human where I go to.

B.en: Tell me about your first trip to another country or city. When did you go? Where did you visit? What did you do there? Who did you go with? Tell me about that trip with lots of details.
cau: I went to China with some colleagues for a business trip 5 years ago.
When I arrived, I was supprised about modern and beauti of China captial: Beijing.
There was so much road, And they are so big.
There're many underground system with high speed.
All around are sky tower.
I also had exciting experience with food there, The local food is so delicious and taste is so good.
It's really a place that I want to come again.
